article.title: Kyiv adapts to new reality of life under constant Russian drone attack
article.description: As a resident of Boryspil, a satellite town of Kyiv, Kostyantyn Kuts has grown accustomed to regular night-time air raids. This past week has been different.
paragraphs: SUPPORT Santa is coming to town! Watch as NORAD tracks Santa live on union-bulletin.com. AP Kyiv adapts to new reality of life under constant Russian drone attack Volodymyr Verbianyi and Olesia Safronova - Bloomberg News (TNS) Sep 5, 2026 Sep 5, 2026 0 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save As a resident of Boryspil, a satellite town of Kyiv, Kostyantyn Kuts has grown accustomed to regular night-time air raids. This past week has been different.

Since late August, Russia has ramped up the frequency of its air assaults on the Ukrainian capital using jet-powered drones that are harder to intercept. With barrages now around the clock rather than mostly at night, life has once again been turned upside down for the city’s more than three million inhabitants.

For Kuts, a 39-year-old neurologist who lives with his wife and two children, travel from his home on the left bank of the Dnipro River to work on the right bank has become impossibly unpredictable as a result of transport disruptions.

“There are no suburban trains, no metro,” he said, adding that a return journey now takes him six or eight hours. At least he is able to use the time productively, making notes, reading professional literature, watching training courses, even consulting remotely. “But it is much worse for patients, for whom medical care will become less accessible due to the inability to get to a doctor,” he said.

The Kremlin’s new tactic has compounded Kyiv’s difficulties, complicating logistics and interrupting public services while increasing the risk of civilian casualties. All this has further eroded morale as the cold season approaches, making many — above all mothers with young children — wonder whether they should leave the exposed city or even the country.

article.title: Kiev security service HQ may have been struck by rival agency - Russian diplomat
article.description: A UAV strike on an SBU building may have been part of a war between Ukrainian security agencies, Russian diplomat Rodion Miroshnik has said Read Full Article at RT.com
paragraphs: Rodion Miroshnik has mocked Vladimir Zelensky for blaming Moscow despite an earlier shootout between Ukrainian intelligence operatives

A drone strike on the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) headquarters in Kiev could have been carried out by the country's military intelligence (HUR) as part of a conflict between the two agencies, high-ranking Russian diplomat Rodion Miroshnik has said.

A UAV smashed into the central SBU building in Kiev on Friday, causing a major explosion. Ukraine's Vladimir Zelensky blamed the strike on Russia, saying the drone had directly targeted the office of the agency's acting head, Aleksandr Poklad. Zelensky said he had tasked Poklad, who was unharmed, with preparing an "adequate, noticeable and, if possible, mirror response."

"According to Zelensky's statement, he maintains that the UAV flying directly into the window of the service's chief was a result of a 'Russian drone' attack, not a showdown between the security agencies provisionally subordinate to him," Miroshnik wrote on Telegram on Friday.
"Zelensky chose the lesser of two evils," he added.

article.title: Israeli Attacks Continue Across Gaza as Humanitarian Crisis Deepens
article.description: In the Gaza Strip, Israeli military violations continued amid escalating humanitarian concerns, while Gaza's Health Ministry reported a rising death to ...
paragraphs: In the Gaza Strip, Israeli military violations continued amid escalating humanitarian concerns, while Gaza’s Health Ministry reported a rising death toll and additional casualties despite the ceasefire that took effect on October 10, 2025.

Medical sources reported that a Palestinian woman died on Saturday evening from wounds sustained in an earlier Israeli attack on the Maghazi refugee camp in central Gaza. They identified her as Latifa Ziad Jabr and said she had been critically injured in an Israeli strike on the refugee camp three months earlier. Her husband, Saqer Abu Karim, was previously killed.

Israeli forces opened fire toward displacement tents in the Sudaniya area of northwestern Gaza, moderately wounding a Palestinian child. In a separate incident, an Israeli airstrike on the Tuffah neighborhood, northeast of Gaza City, injured three Palestinians.

Local sources reported that, before dawn, Israeli quadcopter drones dropped explosive devices near homes on Mushtaha Street and by the Shuja’iyya market, east of Gaza City. No injuries were reported. At the same time, heavy gunfire from Israeli military positions east of the city targeted nearby neighborhoods.

In southern Gaza, Israeli artillery shelled areas northwest of Rafah, while Israeli military vehicles opened heavy fire toward southern parts of Khan Younis. Israeli naval vessels also fired toward the coast of Khan Younis.

REUTERS The Israeli army “kills first, then thinks and tries to find a reason” afterward to justify strikes on the Gaza Strip, said the executive director of Israeli veterans' group Breaking the Silence.

In an interview Friday with France 24 , Nadav Weiman said the army and Israeli authorities seek to “retrospectively” legitimize attacks by attempting to establish links between victims and Hamas or Palestinian Islamic Jihad after strikes have taken place.

“In cases like this Nasser hospital or the 15 paramedics that were killed by IDF (Israeli army) soldiers in Rafah, or air strikes that are killing three-digit numbers of civilians in Gaza ... suddenly the IDF spokesperson in the state of Israel needs to explain to the international community what we did over there and who are the targets for the attack,” Weiman said.

article.title: Israeli army raids 2 West Bank schools on first day of academic year
article.description: Israeli forces threaten school administration south of Nablus, demand removal of Palestinian flag, local sources say | Anadolu
paragraphs: WORLD TÜRKİYE ECONOMY POLITICS ENERGY TECHNOLOGY Middle East Israeli army raids 2 West Bank schools on first day of academic year Israeli forces threaten school administration south of Nablus, demand removal of Palestinian flag, local sources say Layan Bsharat and Sahin Demir 06 September 2026 • Update : 06 September 2026 İSTANBUL The Israeli army raided two schools in the northern occupied West Bank province of Nablus on Sunday as the new academic year began, local sources said.
The sources said Israeli forces entered the grounds of Huwwara Boys Secondary School south of Nablus, threatened the school administration and demanded the removal of the Palestinian flag.
Another Israeli force entered the grounds of Burqa Boys Secondary School northwest of Nablus, with no injuries or arrests reported, according to the sources.

The raids came on the first day of the 2026-2027 academic year, as 846,289 students returned to schools across the occupied West Bank. The students are enrolled in 2,537 government, private and UN-run schools, with around 54,000 teachers.

According to the Palestinian Education Ministry, 634,294 students are enrolled in 1,967 government schools, while 163,787 attend 480 private schools. Another 48,208 students attend 90 schools run by the UN agency for Palestinian refugees (UNRWA).

The killings occurred during a raid in al-Mughayyir on Wednesday. The village has been the site of repeated pogroms by Israeli settlers and forces in recent months.
The Palestinian Wafa news agency, quoting the head of the village council, identified the victims as Mohammad Nassan and Khalil Abu Aliya, both 19 years old.
As residents tried to confront the settlers, Israeli soldiers opened fire on the residents, critically wounding two young men, he said. They later died from their wounds.

The Israeli army raided several areas of the occupied West Bank and Jerusalem on Wednesday, while Israeli settlers destroyed water pipes supplying a Palestinian community in Tubas governorate.

The Jerusalem Governorate said in a statement that an Israeli army force raided the town of al-Ram, north of Jerusalem, and the town of Anata, north-east of the city. No injuries or arrests were reported.
An Israeli army force also raided the city of Nablus in the northern West Bank and patrolled several of its streets and neighbourhoods, according to local sources cited by Anadolu .

(AFP Photo) by Daily Sabah with Agencies Sep 03, 2026 1:16 pm The Israeli military killed two Palestinian teenagers in the occupied West Bank Wednesday night, the Health Ministry said, in an attack the army claimed was its attempt to control an alleged riot.

Omar Mohammad Naji al-Nassan, 19, and Khalil Rasem Khalil Shahada, 16, were shot dead by the Israeli army in the village of al-Mughayyir, northeast of Ramallah in the central West Bank, the ministry said.

Amin Abu Alia, the head of the al-Mughayyir village council, told AFP "Israeli settlers ... tried to steal sheep from two homes" in the village and that following a confrontation, "the Israeli army imposed a siege on the village before raiding its center."
He said the Israeli forces placed snipers inside buildings, who "opened live fire on residents who tried to confront the settlers."

The Israeli army, meanwhile, claimed it had "secured the entrance" to the village "in order to facilitate the return of livestock belonging to Israeli civilians that had been found in the area of the village."

article.title: Israel's Shin Bet Prepared For Months, Used Gaza Informants to Capture Hamas Spy Chief
article.description: "Israeli security officials describe commander of Hamas’s internal security apparatus Muein al-Arabid ... as an “intelligence gold mine"."
paragraphs: “Israeli security officials describe commander of Hamas’s internal security apparatus Muein al-Arabid … as an “intelligence gold mine”.”

Print Facebook Twitter Telegram LinkedIn WhatsApp Email Pinterest Digg Buffer Pocket Blogger Yahoo Mail Flipboard Viber Facebook Messenger Copy Link With Hamas shell-shocked by the daring capture of its spy chief, the Gaza-based Islamist group is trying to piece together how Israel struck right at the heart of its terrorist network.

Muin al-Arabid, who ran Hamas’s spying and repressive security apparatus in Gaza, was successfully nabbed by Israel’s Shin Bet special forces early this week. He is now in Israeli custody and has been described by officials as an “intelligence gold mine” in the war against Hamas terrorism.

Once a feared Hamas enforcer, al-Arabid is already spilling the beans on his former terrorist paymasters. The Times of Israel revealed that “al-Arabid is cooperating with interrogators and providing what is described as valuable information on the terror group’s weapons, personnel and infrastructure in Gaza.”

Israel’s Ynetnews reported that “Hamas is trying to reconstruct how Israeli forces managed to capture one of its most senior internal security officials in the heart of Gaza.” This “involved months of preparation, undercover activity, local informants and even ammunition containing a sedative,” Hamas sources told Arab media.

article.title: Gaza rescuers say Israeli strikes kill five, including two children
article.description: Tragic events in Gaza: authorities report at least five deaths, including two children, due to Israeli fire on Monday.
paragraphs: ARY NEWS brings you 24/7 Live Streaming, Headlines, Bulletins, Talk Shows, Infotainment, and much more.
Add ARY News on Google Photo by OMAR AL-QATTAA / AFP A A Resize Gazan authorities said at least five people were killed by Israeli fire on Monday, including two children.
Two Palestinians were killed at dawn when a tent was bombed in Deir al-Balah, in the central Gaza Strip, according to the civil defence rescue service, which operates under Hamas authority.
A 10-year-old girl was also killed by Israeli artillery fire north of Khan Yunis, in southern Gaza, according to the civil defense and the city’s Nasser Hospital.
The Israeli army told AFP it had no knowledge of the incidents.
